candidates.api_shape: orifice_dashpot(bore, rod_d, orifice_d, stroke, extend_frac) -> {tube, piston, rod} plus c ~ mu*A^2/d^4
candidates.fdm: Tube, piston with a through-hole, rod, two caps. Prints. Fluid is bought. Leak around the piston is the honesty note, same as a printed pump. Air dashpot is the same kit with a smaller hole.
candidates.name: orifice_dashpot
candidates.why: The viscous linear primitive. Door closers, instrument settling, recoil buffers. hydraulic_cylinder is a force source (ports, pressure). This is a rate sink (a hole, no pump). Distinct.

candidates.api_shape: rotary_vane_damper(pot_d, vane_t, sweep_deg, fill) -> {pot, vane, cap}
candidates.fdm: A pot, a vane on a shaft, a cap, bought silicone grease. Prints. Cabinet-door / toilet-seat / steering-damper class. Seal is a bought O-ring.
candidates.name: rotary_vane_damper
candidates.why: The viscous rotary primitive. No current API dissipates rotation. Not a wrap-spring (locks) and not a brake (grounds). Soft-close lids are the agent job.

candidates.api_shape: friction_snubber(pad_a, pad_b, preload) -> two pads + spring, F = mu*N*sign(v)
candidates.fdm: Two printed pads, a belleville or coil preload. Prints. Coulomb, not viscous. Railway snubber / leaf-spring interleaf stand-in.
candidates.name: friction_snubber
candidates.why: Dry friction as a designed sink, not a parasitic way. band_brake grounds a shaft; this is a two-terminal pad pair on a rod or a leaf.

candidates.api_shape: inerter(stroke, flywheel_J, drive='rack'|'screw') -> {term_a, term_b, pinion_or_nut, flywheel} F = b * a_rel
candidates.fdm: Two eyes, a rack or screw, a printed flywheel. Prints. Smith 2002. The two-terminal packaging is the kit; the tooth is rack_pinion.
candidates.name: inerter
candidates.why: Not a damper (no heat) but every modern network draws it next to C and K. Vehicle suspensions, TMDIs. Agents searching inerter currently get nothing. Composition of existing parts, still a named primitive.

candidates.api_shape: bumper(d, h, shape='puck'|'bellows'|'cone') -> one TPU body
candidates.fdm: A printed TPU puck or bellows. The cheapest sink. Progressive if conical.
candidates.name: elastomer_bumper
candidates.why: End-stop / snubber pad. Not a spring (the point is hysteresis and a hard stop). Fine as a one-body kit so agents stop inventing it from cyl.

candidates.api_shape: mass + spring + dashpot on a frame. Frahm 1909
candidates.fdm: Prints as an assembly. A building TMD is a product. A small instrument TMD is composition.
candidates.name: tuned_mass_damper
candidates.why: Named, real, and agents will ask. After dashpot and a mass exist, it is three parts on a plate. Close to a product. Rank after the primitives.

candidates.api_shape: dashpot with air and a check that dumps one way
candidates.fdm: Same envelope as orifice_dashpot plus a check_valve. Pneumatic cushion on a cylinder.
candidates.name: air_cushion
candidates.why: A parameter on the dashpot (fluid=air, plus a check), not a second kit.

candidates.name: eddy_damper
candidates.why: Field device. Same reject as magnetic_gear / magnetic_bearing.

candidates.fdm: Monotube with gas charge, valving, seals. Product.
candidates.name: hydraulic_shock_product
candidates.why: Fox / Bilstein / Koni. The reusable part is orifice_dashpot. The shock is a finished absorber.

candidates.name: brake_as_damper
candidates.why: A brake grounds a shaft to stop it. A damper is a two-terminal rate. Do not merge the shelves.

new_categories.name: dampers
new_categories.why: Energy dissipation is a machinery class. No current shelf. First kits: orifice_dashpot, rotary_vane_damper, friction_snubber, inerter. Brakes ground a shaft; dampers are two-terminal rate elements.

rejected.name: taipei_101_tmd
rejected.why: A building-scale pendulum product. The cell is mass+spring+dashpot.

sources: mechlib/ grep damper|dashpot|snubber|inerter empty; flywheel, coil_spring, hydraulic_cylinder (proposed) are neighbours
summary:
A damper turns organised motion into heat. Norton and machine-design texts split by the dissipation law: viscous (F = c*v, dashpot / rotary vane in a pot), friction (F = mu*N, Coulomb snubber / interleaf), hysteretic / elastomer (loss in the solid), fluid-dynamic (orifice, shock), and field (eddy, MR). Smith 2002 added the inerter (F = b*a_rel), a two-terminal inertia that is not a damper but lives on the same shelf because every textbook now draws C-K-B networks. 507 barely names dissipation (friction brake 242, dynamometer 244, friction test 373). Howell's lossy flexure is a viscoelastic hinge, not a pot. Reuleaux has no damper pair.

Catalog has zero damper APIs. Grep of mechlib/ for damper, dashpot, snubber, inerter, orifice, shock is empty. Neighbours that are not dampers: flywheel (stores, does not dissipate), coil/leaf/wave/belleville (return force rises with x), band_brake (clutches slice, grounds a shaft, not a rate element), linear_way (friction is parasitic). missing-categories already ranked a dampers shelf as med: add it when the first kit lands.

FDM reality. orifice_dashpot is a piston with a hole in a closed cylinder; fluid is bought oil or air; the envelope is tube+piston+rod, cousin of hydraulic_cylinder, but the hole and the sealed volume are the point. rotary_vane_damper is a vane in a silicone-filled pot (cabinet door, toilet seat, steering); prints as a pot + vane + bought grease. friction_snubber is two pads and a preload (Coulomb); prints. elastomer_bumper is a TPU puck or bellows, the cheapest printed sink. inerter is a rack (or leadscrew) spinning a flywheel between two terminals; rack_pinion + flywheel already exist, the kit is the two-terminal packaging. A TMD is mass + spring + dashpot: composition, close to a product once you add the building. Hydraulic monotube shocks, eddy plates, and MR fluid are hardware. Do not file a brake as a damper.
title: Dampers, dashpots, and energy sinks
